BL-2363 - Add missing cache component features
CIS3590 Team 7 - Documentation

Prototype of the core changes:
https://github.com/LivinKevin/BoxLang/tree/BL-2363-add-missing-cache-component-features


1. PROBLEM STATEMENT
--------------------

What issue are we solving?

The cache component (bx:cache / cfcache, Cache.java) declares seven Adobe
ColdFusion attributes but never reads them:

    region, useQueryString, expireURL, username, password, port, protocol

Commit BL-2324 (Apr 2026) removed their NOT_IMPLEMENTED validators, so these
attributes are now silently ignored. CFML code migrated to BoxLang runs
without errors but caches differently than it did in ColdFusion.

Two of them, useQueryString and expireURL, depend on caching by page URL.
BoxLang cannot do that yet: full-page caching is an open TODO in Cache.java,
and the request URL only exists in the web runtime (boxlang-web-support).


2. PROPOSED SOLUTION
--------------------

What changes will be made and why?

Split the work by what each attribute depends on.

Core only (no web dependency, ready now):
  - region: alias for cacheName; cacheName wins if both are passed.
    ACF uses "region" for the same thing, and Cache.java already handles
    aliases this way (id -> key).
  - username, password, port, protocol: accepted and ignored as legacy CFML
    compatibility attributes. In ACF they configured an HTTP request the
    server made to its own page; BoxLang does not cache pages that way.

Core + web-support (after page caching is designed):
  - useQueryString: put the request path, plus the query string when true,
    into generated page cache keys so each URL variation is cached
    separately.
  - expireURL: with action="flush", clear only generated entries whose path
    matches a wildcard pattern, using the existing WildcardFilter.
  - web-support supplies the request path (cgi scope or an event).

Related fix found during the investigation:
  - web-support's clientcache/servercache handler listens on the event
    onComponentInvocation, but core announces onCacheComponentAction, so the
    handler likely never runs. This should be wired correctly before page
    caching is built on top of it.


3. IMPLEMENTATION STEPS
-----------------------

Step 1 - region and legacy attributes (core, Cache.java)
  - In _invoke(): if cacheName is null, use the region attribute.
  - Group username, password, port, protocol under a "Legacy CFML
    compatibility attributes - accepted but not used" comment.
  - Document all five in the Javadoc above _invoke().

Step 2 - Fix the event wiring (core or web-support, maintainers to choose)
  - Rename WebRequest.onComponentInvocation to onCacheComponentAction, or
    have core announce onComponentInvocation.

Step 3 - Design page caching (core + web-support)
  - Decide how a cached page is identified, whether its URL is stored in the
    key or in entry metadata, and how a full response is captured and
    replayed.

Step 4 - useQueryString (core + web-support)
  - Generated keys become BL_TEMPLATE_<path>[?query]|<hash>.
  - Path comes from cgi.script_name and cgi.query_string.
  - Outside a web request, keys stay exactly as they are today.

Step 5 - expireURL (core, Cache.java, case FLUSH)
  - clearAll( new WildcardFilter( "BL_TEMPLATE_" + expireURL + "*" ) )

Step 6 - Documentation
  - Update the @attribute Javadoc lines and remove the
    "TODO: These are specfic to web connectivity..." comment.

Steps 1, 4 (core side) and 5 are prototyped on the team branch above.


4. VALIDATION PLAN
------------------

Tests to add/update
  Core - src/test/java/ortus/boxlang/runtime/components/cache/CacheTest.java
  (prototyped on the team branch):
    - testRegionAttribute: put/get with region stores in the named cache
    - testCacheNameBeatsRegion: cacheName wins when both are passed
    - testLegacyAttributesIgnored: legacy attributes do not break put/get
    - testUseQueryStringOutsideWebRequest: content caching unchanged
      outside a web request
    - testExpireURL: flush removes only entries matching the pattern
  web-support (to add, using MockHTTPExchange / BaseWebTest):
    - useQueryString true vs false with ?id=1 and ?id=2
    - clientcache / servercache set the Cache-Control header

Verification steps
  1. ./gradlew spotlessApply
  2. ./gradlew test --tests "*CacheTest*", then the full ./gradlew test
  3. Build the core jar locally and run web-support's tests against it
  4. Manual check in a web app: load page.cfm?id=1 and ?id=2 with
     useQueryString on and off, then flush with expireURL

Success criteria
  - All seven attributes have defined, documented and tested behavior
  - All existing cache tests still pass
  - Generated keys are unchanged outside a web request
  - Behavior matches the Adobe ColdFusion cfcache reference
  - Maintainers approve the core / web-support split
